title: Past-Due Interest Reserve in Operating Lines of Credit Advances
content:
Billed interest left unpaid past its due date on one of the Operating Lines of Credit is held back from what the line will advance, in full or in part depending on how far past due the latest bill is.

## Rule

A past-due reserve is taken off:

- **all the billed interest not yet paid** when the latest bill's due date is more than the product's grace days, in calendar days, past;
- **0.5 of it** when that due date has passed by no more than the product's grace days;
- **nothing** when no billed interest is unpaid or the latest bill is not yet due.

The billed interest not yet paid is the interest billed on the line plus interest payments returned unpaid less interest payments, rounded to cents. The latest bill is the line's interest bill with the latest due date; days past are counted from that due date, the due date itself being day 0. The reserve is taken off the lending limit together with the outstanding principal.

## Grace days by product

| Product | Grace days |
|---|---|
| StartRight Operating Line | 15 |
| ExpressLine Operating Credit | 15 |
| Seasonal Operating Loan | 15 |
| Revolving Operating Line | 15 |
| Borrowing Base Operating Line | 10 |
| Agribusiness Revolving Line | 10 |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical Revolving Operating Line, USD 3,000 of billed interest unpaid, latest bill due 15 April)

| Date of the request | Days past the due date | Reserve |
|---|---|---|
| 14 April | not yet due | Nothing |
| 15 April | 0 — the due date itself | Nothing |
| 16 April | 1 | USD 1,500 |
| 30 April | 15 | USD 1,500 |
| 1 May | 16 | USD 3,000 |
